items.title: Geoff Bull Interview, 1966-05-05
items.q: The fact that they'll use Harry Shields, and not John Handy, is, is ridiculous, because Harry Shields is quite a nice clarinet player, but he's just nothing compared to John Handy as a New Orleans musician.

ctx.x: No, we can restrict anything you want us to, speak your mind. Well, I mean, you know, you know what I mean, you know.

I know exactly what you mean. The fact that they'll use clarinet players like, now, uh, um, not taking anything against him, because I quite like his playing, and he did play some nice things, but the fact that they'll use a clarinet player like Polo Barnes in Preservation Hall, and not use a saxophone player like John Handy, to me, is rubbish, because John Handy is, is, is just so much better, that it isn't funny.
